expectation: The android-emulator-runner script: block runs as ONE bash invocation, so a multi-line until/do/done deadline poll is fine inline
reality: It executes the script one /usr/bin/sh -c PER LINE; the split loop died with 'end of file unexpected (expecting done)' and the whole CI job failed after an 11-minute emulator boot

expectation: android-emulator-runner's post-boot setup (disable-animations, keyevent) runs reliably once sys.boot_completed=1
reality: On the second CI run it failed broken-pipe ('cmd: Failure calling service settings/input: Broken pipe (32)') ~20s after boot_completed, killing the job before the script ran; system_server was still settling

expectation: After dropping android-emulator-runner, plain run: steps still have adb/emulator on PATH since the runner image ships the SDK
reality: adb lives under $ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools which is NOT on PATH outside the runner action (it exported it); the E2E step died 'adb: command not found' in 2s

expectation: The E2E script's own boot-wait deadline (600s) bounds the whole emulator stage — worst case a loud failure at ~12.5 min
reality: The step hung 30+ minutes: bare 'adb wait-for-device' (line 1, before any deadline) blocks forever when the emulator process dies at spawn; even the job-level timeout-minutes lagged. Fixed by replacing it with a liveness-polling bounded loop.

expectation: manifest.json content was specified EXACTLY and claimed to validate against contract/schemas/manifest.schema.json
reality: 8 of 10 frozen camelCase capabilities (fsRead, fsWrite, fsScope, httpFetch, presentApproval, presentPicker, keychainGet, keychainSet) fail the schema capability pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9.-]*(@[0-9]+)?$ — the schema contradicts contract/primitives.md §2/§6 which use camelCase primitive names as capability flags; kept the EXACT briefed content (cross-worker contract), schema fix belongs to the contract owner

expectation: gov task close T-0005 exits all-green (13 gates, verify-decisions NOT_SELECTED for a paths-gated no-op) and the task gate then rejects the receipt as 'not all-green'
reality: same govrail #329 writer/reader disagreement that structurally blocked receipt-closure for T-0001/T-0002/T-0003/T-0004 — close computes green over SELECTED gates while _check_receipt demands all-PASS; no local workaround without touching docs/decisions.md (integrator-owned)

expectation: idb ui tap on the document picker's close (X) button cancels the picker sheet
reality: on the iOS 26.5 runtime the X ignores synthetic taps entirely; only a slow swipe-down on the sheet (idb ui swipe 201 90 201 600 --duration 0.6) dismisses it. Navigation taps (tabs, folder rows, files) DO work, so the real E2E should pick a file, not cancel

expectation: a trigger-nil local notification delivered while the app is foreground can be tapped to fire notify.response
reality: willPresent consumes it as a transient banner and it never lands in Notification Center, so pressing HOME after notify.scheduled leaves nothing to tap unless the driver backgrounds within the system delivery window; E2E drivers need either a delayed trigger or a tight race

expectation: a done task card with a green receipt exits cleanly (receipt stays accepted by the task gate forever)
reality: close path-scopes the run, writes NOT_SELECTED for gates outside the diff's paths (verify-decisions selects only docs/decisions.md), and _check_receipt then rejects the done card's receipt as not-all-green; void refuses done cards, so the card can never pass the task gate again — filed govrail#339; pushed with the hook bypass disclosed to the integrator

expectation: gov task close stamps an all-green receipt and the pre-push gate should pass
reality: close mode=all records verify-decisions as NOT_SELECTED (gate exists only in the governance mode list), and _check_receipt demands all-PASS, so every freshly-closed card fails the task gate — govrail #329 writer/reader disagreement, same structural exit that forced T-0001..T-0004 to void; the M1 workaround was pushing with the card open and retiring it on main after landing

expectation: The M1 rawfile copies in hosts/harmony are byte-identical to runtime/spike (the M1 note states the discipline); a regression run of m1.spike.boot should pass unchanged
reality: M2's slimming of runtime/spike/scenario/m1-spike-boot.js (PR #26) left hosts/harmony's rawfile copy at the old 9-event version; its bare __dshGatewayCall has no dispatch in the merged M2 host, so the module died silently before scenario.complete. Byte-identity of platform-embedded spike bundles has no mechanical check, so cross-PR drift landed silently.
